units.source_text: 我慢慢学会了河童日常讲的语言，也渐渐了解了河童的风俗习惯。

en.t: Little by little, I learned the language the kappa used in daily life, and gradually came to understand their customs and habits.

units.source_text: 可是，其中有一个让我很费解的荒唐的习惯：

en.t: But among them was one absurd custom that I found very hard to understand:

units.source_text: 人类认为严肃正经的事，河童却觉得是笑话；

en.t: Things that human beings regard as solemn and serious, the kappa consider jokes;

units.source_text: 而人类觉得是笑话的事儿，河童却当做严肃正经的事儿。

en.t: and things that human beings think are jokes, the kappa treat as solemn and serious matters.

units.source_text: 诸如说，人类认为正义、人道之类的是天经地义的；

en.t: For example, human beings believe that things like justice and humanity are natural and self-evident;

units.source_text: 但是河童却觉得这些十分可笑。

en.t: but the kappa find such things extremely laughable.

units.source_text: 总的来说，它们对滑稽可笑的看法，和人类完全相反。

en.t: In short, their sense of what is comic and ridiculous is the complete opposite of that of human beings.

units.source_text: 有一次，我和查喀医生说起计划生育的事儿，查喀笑的夹鼻眼镜差点掉下来。

en.t: Once, when I spoke with Doctor Chack about birth control, Chack laughed so hard that his pince-nez nearly fell off.

units.source_text: 毫无疑问我生气了，于是质问他为什么笑。

en.t: Naturally, I became angry, and so I demanded to know why he was laughing.

units.source_text: 我记忆里查喀是这样说的——也许我的记忆会有点偏差，

en.t: As I remember it, Chack said the following, though my memory may be somewhat mistaken,

units.source_text: 因为当时我对河童语言还不是特别精通。

en.t: because at the time I was not yet especially proficient in the kappa language.
